text:
jamal: quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — can we do a short thread about hybrid lease lifecycle + backpressure behaviors? trying to capture open tradeoffs.

alex: yep, outline the main questions and we can pick which to tackle.

jamal: main things i care about: 1) when to convert a soft lease -> hard reservation, 2) how much headroom to keep for kv cache rebuilds, 3) signal propagation latency for preemptive throttles.

maria: + how do we avoid oscillation on bursty tenants? we saw a small loop in the simulation yesterday.

lee: notes from sim: if soft->hard threshold is too low we pin capacity and starvation spans increase for others. if too high, latency SLOs for the origin tenant degrade.

alex: maybe two knobs: conversion_threshold (ms of sustained queueing) and hysteresis_window (seconds). keep them independent so SRE can tune.

jamal: agreed. proposed defaults: conversion_threshold=150ms sustained for 3 windows, hysteresis_window=30s. then allow lease_decay back to soft after 60s of under-threshold.

maria: that matches intuition. we should also account for kv-cache rebuild cost: when a hard lease gets preempted, rebuilding KVCACHE adds ~40-120ms depending on model. we should reserve headroom to avoid repeated rebuilds.

lee: can we do headroom accounting like: reserved_tokens = max(estimated_kv_rebuild_tokens, min_headroom) and subtract from admission_budget? keeps eviction predictable.

jamal: example pseudo:
````
if soft_lease and sustained_queue >= conversion_threshold:
  promote_to_hard()
  headroom = max(kv_rebuild_est, min_headroom)
  admission_budget -= headroom
````
(4 backticks to mimic a fenced block)

alex: + add a fast-path: tiny requests (<8 tokens) skip promotion to avoid thrashing microbursts.

maria: telemetry: emit lease_state transitions and kv_rebuild_est when we promote. need trace id to correlate with token-level latency spikes.

lee: also we should surface a preempt_hint metric: when a tenant is within X% of its soft limit repeatedly, we send a hint to the router to divert new low-priority requests. keeps queues smooth.

jamal: question: how quickly should routers act on preempt_hint? immediate would reduce tail but may increase cold starts. maybe rate-limit hints to 1/s per tenant.

alex: +1 rate-limit. and treat hints as advisory — routers can apply probabilistic drop or route-to-fallback depending on SLO tier.

maria: thought on oscillation: use randomized backoff on decay windows per tenant instance to avoid synchronized fallbacks across pods. add a jitter +/- 15% to decay timers.

lee: edge-case: if multiple tenants promote at the same time due to a global burst, we need a fairness arbiter. suggest a short-lived admission token auction: each tenant bids with priority_score and we allocate slot slices proportional to score for the next N windows.

jamal: auction idea seems heavy but could be a separate follow-up. for now let's pick a soft fairness: inverse-proportional decrement to admission_budget when we see multi-tenant promotions.

dev-bot: CI check: rtscheduler/tests/sim_hybrid_lifecycle.py: PASS (12/12)

alex: next steps: jamal to draft a thin RFC with the knobs + telemetry + default values. maria to add KVCACHE rebuild estimator; lee to add preempt_hint API on router. we'll sync in 48h.

jamal: noted. i'll post the draft + sim results to the RFC channel. thanks all :thumbsup:
